claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and any children you're claiming for.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for? If so, could you please tell me their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. My son Alex is 19 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I appreciate you providing Alex's age, as this is relevant to Child Benefit eligibility.

Before I can give you a definitive answer, I need to gather a bit more information about Alex's circumstances.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education. He's doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's helpful information.

**Does Alex receive any income from employment, such as wages or salary?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work. He's focused on his studies full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's useful to know.

**Does Alex live with you, or does he live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me just gather one more important detail.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status in the UK? Also, do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, I'm settled here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. I have all the details I need to assess your eligibility. Let me check the official Child Benefit eligibility rules to ensure I give you an accurate answer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on the official Child Benefit eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's a summary of why:

- **Age**: Alex is 19 years old, which is under 20
- **Education**: He's in full-time A-level education at sixth form college, which counts as approved education
- **Living arrangements**: He lives with you at home
- **Residence & status**: You live in the UK with settled status
- **Work/benefits**: He doesn't work or receive benefits in his own right

As long as Alex continues in approved education and doesn't start working 24 hours or more per week or claim certain benefits, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him. If his circumstances change - for example, if he completes his A-levels and doesn't continue into further approved education or training, or if he starts working significantly - you should inform HMRC as this could affect your eligibility.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

According to the eligibility rules, you normally still qualify for Child Benefit if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training, which applies to Alex.
